sections.heading: Pay attention deliberately
sections.content: Before evaluating founders, remind yourself to watch for subtle cues. In the conversation, notice whether the co-founders seem to get along, whether founders understand their product, and whether they become defensive. Livingston said there are no trick questions: the point is to pay attention.

sections.heading: Ask, then reflect
sections.content: Use a simple checklist in your head, then take time afterward to consider what you observed. For example, ask how the founders’ product is better than a competitor’s and reflect on how they handled the question. If you don’t know their history, ask how they met, whether they have worked together before, and how it is going. She recommended being more conscious about these questions because they can reveal information relevant to the investment decision.
